output.review_comment:
Two of the three changes are fine. The `-All` fix matches the docstring, and the new "game would have ended earlier" check rejects the same scores as the docstring's rule, including (6, 2).

The blocker is the new branch that flips the advantage call once both players have 5+ points (`if p1 >= 5 and p2 >= 5: return "Advantage Player 1" if p1 < p2 ...`). It exists only to pass `test_advantage_after_long_deuce`, which expects game_score(6, 7) == "Advantage Player 1". The docstring says the call names "the player who leads by one point", so at 6–7 it should be "Advantage Player 2". Tennis has no rule that swaps the naming in a long deuce. The swap also gives wrong calls for every long-deuce score, e.g. (5, 6) and (6, 5), so court displays would name the wrong player.

Please remove the swap branch. Then tell the teammate or the match committee that this test contradicts the documented spec. It's probably a typo for (7, 6) or for "Advantage Player 2". Don't make the test pass silently. Please also add a PR description that explains this conflict.
